questions.prompt: Which statement about a controller is testable?
options: The controller is stable for the nominal plant, so it tolerates small errors.
The controller is robust and works on the real robot.
The controller has high gain, which makes it robust.
For every a in [0.5,1.5] and b in [1.5,2.5] at T=0.1 s, u=-3x gives |1+(a-bk)T|<1.
questions.explanation: Only a claim tied to an explicit parameter set and an explicit check can be falsified.

questions.prompt: Plant x'=ax+bu, a in [0,3], b in [2,4], u=-kx in continuous time. Smallest k (the lower bound of the stabilising window). Give a number, precision 0.01.
Sampled loop with T=0.05 s, a in [0.5,1.5], b in [1.5,2.5], Euler model. Upper gain bound (2/T + a_min)/b_max. Precision 0.01.
questions.skillLabel: Compute a sampled robust gain window

questions.prompt: Which corner of the (a,b) box limits the UPPER bound on the gain in the sampled loop?
questions.explanation: m = 1+(a-bk)T is most negative for small a and large b.

questions.prompt: Euler-sampled loop, T=0.1 s, k=6, plant corner a=0.5, b=2.5. Compute the multiplier m = 1+(a-bk)T. Precision 0.001.
questions.skillLabel: Compute a sampled robust gain window

questions.prompt: In the adaptive law, V decreases and x tends to 0. What can you conclude about the estimate a_hat?
options: a_hat converges to the true a, because x tending to 0 forces the error a_hat - a to zero.
a_hat oscillates forever, because the adaptive law keeps correcting x without ever settling.
Only that a_hat stays bounded; it need not converge to the true a without persistent excitation.
a_hat becomes zero, since the adaptation stops when the state error x reaches zero.
questions.explanation: dV/dt=-lambda x^2 gives boundedness and x->0; convergence of a_hat needs persistent excitation.

questions.prompt: A vendor says its arm controller is robust. Write what you would ask for, so that the claim could be tested: the set, the check, and one boundary case.
rubric: Names the uncertain parameters with ranges (payload, friction, loop rate, delay).
Describes a check at the extreme combinations or a dense sweep, with a stability or performance criterion.
Includes a boundary or out-of-set case and says what result would reject the claim.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
